title: Simplicial tensors and cotensors by universal elements
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category enriched over $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with associative composition, identity vertices and underlying morphisms identified with mapping-set vertices. Chosen simplicial tensors and cotensors consist of objects $K\otimes X$ and $Y^K$ for every small simplicial set $K$ and objects $X,Y$, together with universal simplicial maps $\eta_{K,X}:K\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,K\otimes X)$ and $\epsilon_{K,Y}:K\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(Y^K,Y)$. Require the maps induced by composition with these elements and cartesian-closed currying to be isomorphisms of simplicial sets:
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(K\otimes X,Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}[K,\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,Y)],\qquad \underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,Y^K)\xrightarrow{\sim}[K,\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,Y)].$$
Here the first comparison curries $(k,a)\mapsto a\eta_{K,X}(k)$ and the second curries $(k,b)\mapsto\epsilon_{K,Y}(k)b$; they are enriched natural by the composition laws. The tensor of $f:X\to Y$ is the unique map $K\otimes f:K\otimes X\to K\otimes Y$ corresponding under the first representing isomorphism on vertices to the simplicial map $K\xrightarrow{\eta_{K,Y}}\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(Y,K\otimes Y)\xrightarrow{f^*}\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,K\otimes Y)$. These data express the enriched natural tensor and cotensor adjunctions.

source.place: Categorical Homotopy Theory, Definitions 3.7.2 and 3.7.3 and Remark 3.7.4, printed p.38 (PDF p.53); enriched universal-element formulation by composition and the enriched Yoneda lemma.
